name: moss
description: A quiet, restorative identity for a botanical skincare studio. Generous negative space meets a sculptural leaf and an unexpectedly fresh chartreuse.
heading: manrope
rules: Keep the leaf upright and give it half its height in clear space.
Use forest for text; new leaf is a supporting surface, never small text on oat.
Let the oversized mark crop at the edge of photography or packaging.

name: orbit
description: An exploratory identity for a collaborative ideas platform. Orbital geometry, lilac space, and wide-set typography create a world that feels one step ahead.
heading: space-grotesk
rules: Orbit rings stay at a 28-degree inclination.
Use lilac as the primary canvas and deep space for the wordmark.
Keep interface components rounded while display layouts remain open.

name: SORA
description: A considered identity for a light-led architecture practice. A blue doorway, measured capitals, and a strict alignment system give every application room to breathe.
heading: outfit
rules: Align the arch opening to the baseline of the wordmark.
Set headings in spaced capitals and body copy in sentence case.
Build compositions on an eight-column grid with wide outside margins.

name: OFFSCRIPT
description: A rule-bending system for an independent creative studio. A cut-paper asterisk, electric orange, and deliberately displaced type make it impossible to ignore.
heading: archivo
voice: Direct, irreverent, and full of conviction.
rules: Keep the asterisk sharp; do not round its ends.
Oversized type may break the grid, but utility text must align precisely.
Use hot orange as a dominant surface, paired only with ink for text.

name: bloom
description: An exuberant identity for everyday objects that make people smile. Rounded petals, juicy coral, and soft lilac turn a small moment into something memorable.
heading: bricolage
voice: Sunny, conversational, and a little cheeky.
rules: Petals may rotate as a group, but their proportions never change.
Mix two pastel surfaces per layout with berry as the text anchor.
Use pill-shaped labels as playful annotations, not primary headings.

name: AUREL
tagline: The art of taking your time.
description: A warm, cultivated identity for a small hotel with a big sense of place. A radiating sun seal, a refined serif, and wine-colored details suggest understated luxury.
heading: cormorant
rules: The sun seal sits above the wordmark, never inside it.
Reserve gilded for ornaments and spacious surfaces; use bordeaux for body text.
Pair large serif headings with very small, tracked sans-serif labels.

name: fieldwork
description: A practical outdoor identity inspired by contour maps and trail journals. Rugged olive, rust, and a horizon mark connect useful gear to the places it goes.
heading: work-sans
voice: Resourceful, observant, and down to earth.
rules: Use contour lines as full-bleed backgrounds at low visual density.
Keep the horizon mark horizontal even on angled applications.
Give product specifications mono typography and clearly separated rows.

name: neue
description: A restrained digital identity built around a folded N and a cool mineral palette. Every line has a job; every layout prioritizes clarity over decoration.
heading: dm-sans
rules: The folded N is always filled, never outlined.
Use a single accent per interface view and maintain strong neutral hierarchy.
Align all headings to the same vertical axis across a page.

name: Paloma
description: A literary identity with a distinctive paper-bird emblem. Mustard yellow and midnight blue frame a graceful serif, bringing an independent press to life.
heading: lora
rules: Let the bird point toward the reading direction.
Use marigold for covers and midnight for all long-form reading text.
Set excerpts with generous leading and a visible opening margin.

name: goodkind
tagline: A little good goes a long way.
description: A generous identity for a neighborhood mutual-aid collective. A smiling loop, surprising tomato red, and friendly typography make participation feel easy.
heading: rubik
rules: The smile remains open at the top; do not turn it into a closed badge.
Write calls to action in everyday language and sentence case.
Use lavender and tomato in separate blocks, with plum linking the layout.

name: RELAY
description: A high-energy identity for real-time infrastructure. A stepped signal, acid yellow, and compact technical typography communicate speed without visual clutter.
heading: unbounded
rules: Use the three-step signal at fixed proportions.
Acid yellow carries action; terminal carries technical detail.
Number modules and keep specification labels in monospaced capitals.

name: Sundaze
description: A nostalgic identity for a neighborhood coffee-and-soda bar. A rising sun, warm apricot stripes, and a delightfully soft serif bring the slow weekend to every day.
heading: fraunces
rules: Keep sunrise bands parallel and evenly spaced.
Use roast for text on apricot or cream soda surfaces.
Give headline typography a soft curve through generous spacing, not distortion.

name: onda
description: A fluid identity for a coastal movement studio. Hand-drawn wave geometry, ocean blue, and cloud-white surfaces create a calm but active visual rhythm.
heading: urbanist
rules: Wave strokes retain rounded caps and never taper.
Allow organic bands to flow off both sides of the canvas.
Use sea glass for generous background areas, not paragraph text.

name: Elsewhere
description: An evocative identity for thoughtful travel journals. A doorway into another world, pale persimmon, and an expressive serif invite people to take the scenic route.
heading: instrument-serif
rules: The doorway is a window, so leave its center visually open.
Frame photography with a generous postcard border.
Use large serif headlines and small, uppercase location captions.

name: FORMHAUS
description: A structural identity for a furniture workshop. Intersecting beams, a deep ultramarine, and a strict modular grid make the construction itself the visual language.
heading: syne
rules: Build all graphic frames from the same beam thickness.
Let ultramarine dominate with plywood as the counterweight.
Keep titles flush left and attach measurements to visible grid lines.

name: velour
description: A tactile identity for a slow-fashion label. A looping ribbon, soft blush, and precise charcoal wordmarks balance romantic detail with a contemporary silhouette.
heading: prata
rules: Preserve the ribbon's negative space at every size.
Use rouge as a tiny editorial punctuation rather than a full background.
Keep garment information quiet and never track body paragraphs.

name: kinfolk
description: A generous identity for a local produce pantry. A growing sprout, butter-yellow paper, and an honest serif connect familiar food with the people who grow it.
heading: fraunces
rules: The sprout grows upward with a visible stem.
Use butter labels with olive text on natural packaging.
Treat ingredient lists as a key part of the design, not fine print.

name: modo
description: A clear identity for a small-business finance tool. Interlocking modules and a single decisive cobalt accent create a system that feels both trustworthy and approachable.
heading: manrope
rules: Keep a one-module gap between the two halves of the symbol.
Use cobalt for active elements, with ledger for long-form text.
Align numerical values to the right and use consistent decimal precision.

name: juno
description: A lively identity for an independent accessories label. Four offset dots, violet blocks, and a confident rounded wordmark celebrate personal expression without taking it too seriously.
heading: outfit
rules: Keep the dot cluster asymmetrical rather than arranging it in a square.
Let violet and limeade meet at hard-edged background divisions.
Use oversized lowercase words and short, friendly supporting lines.

name: RASTER
description: A digital-first identity for a motion and code studio. A broken pixel diamond, cold neutrals, and a flicker of acid green create an unmistakable computational character.
heading: space-grotesk
rules: Pixel shapes snap to a square grid without rounded corners.
Use phosphor to identify one focal point per composition.
Set captions as compact mono data labels at the canvas edges.

name: Commonroom
description: A civic identity for shared neighborhood spaces. An open-table symbol, dependable blue, and warm paper typography make events and information feel genuinely accessible.
heading: bricolage
rules: Keep the open center of the table mark clear.
Use visible rules to organize notices and event dates.
Information hierarchy takes priority over expressive headline placement.

name: Caravan
tagline: The long way is the good way.
description: A wandering identity for a road-trip outfitter. A rolling pennant, burnt sienna, and sturdy vintage lettering bring practical adventure back into focus.
heading: bebas
rules: The pennant always points right and uses the full-height mast.
Frame display headlines with badge-like rules and a small route label.
Use roadside teal sparingly against the warm main palette.

name: Halcyon
description: A contemplative identity for a restorative retreat. Concentric rings, pale rose, and finely drawn serif typography create a visual pause in an otherwise noisy world.
heading: instrument-serif
rules: Concentric rings share one center and a consistent stroke width.
Use stillness for the majority of every canvas.
Leave at least one-third of each composition free of content.

name: MONUMENT
description: A solid identity for an urban design practice. Stacked concrete-like blocks and wide black typography create presence through proportion rather than ornament.
heading: unbounded
rules: Stacked blocks retain their stepped silhouette.
Use a visible structural grid and thick section rules.
Keep copper confined to identifiers or a single small module.

name: nori
description: A light identity for a plant-forward lunch spot. A curled seaweed mark, gentle mint, and a sharp little splash of salmon balance organic warmth with urban energy.
heading: rubik
rules: The kelp mark is one continuous silhouette.
Organize menus into softly bounded bento-like modules.
Use ginger to highlight seasonal items, never to imply warnings.

name: tandem
description: A balanced identity for a shared-mobility platform. Two linked loops, a clean teal, and functional typography express connection through the simplest possible geometry.
heading: urbanist
rules: Both loops use equal dimensions and a shared baseline.
Keep interface spacing on a four-unit rhythm.
Use petrol text on porcelain for route and journey information.

name: pebble
description: A friendly identity for a habit-building app. Irregular rounded stones, clear cornflower blue, and an expressive but readable wordmark make progress feel human.
heading: bricolage
rules: Use asymmetrical pebbles rather than perfect circles.
Never visually rank people; use color to distinguish habits instead.
Keep encouraging headlines short and in lowercase.

name: PHASE
description: An energetic identity for a development toolkit. An interrupted diagonal, electric turquoise, and sharply cut compositions express progress as an ongoing transition.
heading: syne
rules: Diagonal shapes share a 35-degree angle.
Use dark mode as the dominant developer-facing background.
Highlight a single transition with ion instead of adding gradients.

name: Almanac
description: A thoughtful identity for an independent culture journal. An open-book emblem, deeply inked green, and index-like labels bring a sense of discovery to long-form stories.
heading: playfair
rules: The open book retains a clearly visible central spine.
Use issue numbers and running headers as integral design elements.
Combine serif titles with sans-serif paragraphs and mono-style metadata.

name: mellow
tagline: Take the day as it comes.
description: An easygoing identity for home goods and good moods. A soft four-point sparkle, warm peach fields, and wonderfully chunky type recall the optimism of a slower era.
heading: fraunces
rules: Sparkles use soft inward curves, never sharp straight spokes.
Keep backgrounds warm and use mulberry to anchor the composition.
Set short, chunky headlines with tight spacing and spacious supporting copy.

name: Atelier No.8
tagline: Objects with a point of view.
description: A precise identity for a collectible-object atelier. A faceted diamond, antique mauve, and high-contrast serif lettering lend small editions a sense of enduring value.
heading: cormorant
rules: Keep diamond facets outlined at a consistent weight.
Use edition numbers and object dimensions as deliberate typographic details.
Allow old gold only as a line or a small seal.

name: UNFOLD
description: An uncompromising identity for a design publication. Folded paper geometry, bright yellow, and dense display typography turn the printed page into a graphic object.
heading: archivo
rules: Fold lines remain visible and meet at exact corners.
Run headlines across the page while captions stay in fixed columns.
Use yellow to designate primary editorial content, not decorative accents.

name: terra
tagline: Made of the places we love.
description: A material-led identity for a sustainable building studio. A layered hill, clay-rich color, and tactile typographic contrast put landscapes at the heart of the system.
heading: lora
rules: Hill layers are offset but share one continuous lower edge.
Build compositions from horizontal strata with unequal heights.
Use earth text on limestone for all technical explanations.

name: interval
description: A lucid identity for a focus and rest app. Two separated bars, inky navy, and measured whitespace give a simple pause a meaningful visual presence.
heading: outfit
rules: The space between pause bars equals one bar width.
Let whitespace communicate rest instead of adding decorative calm imagery.
Use one concise message per view and keep secondary information small.

name: pippa
tagline: A bite of the bright side.
description: A candy-bright identity for a small bakery. A playful bow, pink blocks, and sunny yellow surprises make every box feel like a present before it is even opened.
heading: rubik
rules: Bow loops stay full and symmetrical while the tails may crop.
Use jam for nutritional details and all small text.
Treat product names as big, cheerful headlines rather than labels.

name: VERTEX
description: A kinetic identity for electric mobility. A pointed shard, deep violet, and a directional compositional system suggest momentum before anything moves.
heading: unbounded
rules: Use forward-facing shards with a shared vanishing direction.
Keep technical details on calm surfaces separate from kinetic graphics.
Ignition is a small action accent, not a body-text color.

name: Marginalia
tagline: The interesting things at the edges.
description: A personal identity for a research and writing studio. Expressive brackets, lilac notes, and an elegant reading serif turn annotations into the star of the system.
heading: instrument-serif
rules: Brackets frame a thought without closing it in.
Use a deliberately wide margin for notes and secondary commentary.
Keep long reading text on manuscript white, with lilac as an annotation field.

name: Supergood
description: A cheerful identity for a maker community. A chunky check, minty teal, and sunny vintage typography turn workshops and small victories into something worth celebrating.
heading: bricolage
rules: The check keeps its chunky rectangular construction.
Use a checkerboard only as a border or a dedicated graphic surface.
Headlines should sound like an invitation from a friend.

name: SEREIN
description: A poetic identity for a late-night tea salon. A fine crescent, midnight blue, and warm champagne-colored paper create a distinctive mood of intimate sophistication.
heading: prata
rules: The crescent opens to the right and retains a fine inner curve.
Use tracked capitals for the wordmark, never for paragraphs.
Let champagne lines and borders remain subtle against after dark.

name: ASSEMBLY
description: A participatory identity for an urban arts collective. Four fitted pieces, energetic citron, and type that behaves like signage turn many voices into one strong system.
heading: bebas
rules: The four fitted pieces must remain distinguishable.
Use sign-like large capitals and keep event details in consistent blocks.
Citron surfaces carry workshop-colored text for accessible contrast.

name: wildroot
description: A grounded identity for regenerative gardening tools. Branching roots, mulberry soil tones, and softly rustic type honor the untidy beauty of things that grow.
heading: fraunces
rules: The branching root symbol always has a visible central stem.
Allow branches to frame content without crossing body text.
Use husk for instructional pages and wild grass for packaging.

name: still
description: A pared-back identity for durable household essentials. One grounded oval, sandstone neutrals, and effortless geometric type create a system designed to age well.
heading: work-sans
rules: Keep the grounded oval at a fixed 3:2 proportion.
Use tonal contrast rather than additional decorative colors.
Product names are sentence case with plainly stated materials beneath.

name: fizz!
description: A fizzy identity for a botanical soda label. A bouncing burst, tangerine orange, and high-impact rounded typography make a tiny can feel full of personality.
heading: outfit
rules: The burst uses alternating spoke lengths and a clear central dot.
Keep flavor information in distinct color blocks.
The exclamation point is part of the wordmark and should never be omitted.

name: AXIOM
tagline: A foundation for what is next.
description: A systematic identity for an open research platform. An impossible triangle, icy blue, and precisely tracked text suggest complexity made understandable.
heading: space-grotesk
rules: The three sides of the triangle use matching thickness.
Blueprint lines should support structure, not compete with content.
Use glacier for diagram fields and deep logic for explanatory text.

name: Folio
tagline: Every page has a point of view.
description: A cultured identity for a portfolio and essay platform. An offset page corner, terracotta ink, and generous serif headlines make individual work feel carefully presented.
heading: lora
rules: Page corners appear as open right angles, never closed boxes.
Use a vertical rule to separate project metadata from descriptions.
Give each featured work a full-width reading area and clear attribution.

name: Daytrip
description: A spirited identity for local travel guides. A rolling compass, sunshine yellow, and friendly mid-century display type make nearby adventures feel like a special occasion.
heading: fraunces
rules: Compass points align vertically even when the surrounding badge rotates.
Use ticket-style borders with route information in a distinct lower strip.
Place sunshine behind short display headlines, not long itineraries.

name: Maison Lune
description: A romantic identity for a guesthouse and table. A moonlit window, pale blue-gray, and beautifully balanced serif type turn a stay into a quiet ritual.
heading: playfair
rules: The moonlit window keeps its central division and open lower space.
Use brass only for fine lines, seals, or room identifiers.
Center invitation headlines while keeping practical information left aligned.

name: OUTLIER
description: An independent identity for experimental streetwear. A displaced square, bold rust-red fields, and sharply condensed typography champion the beauty of not fitting in.
heading: bebas
rules: One square is deliberately displaced; the rest remain on the grid.
Use condensed display type at dramatic scale without stretching glyphs.
Keep care instructions plain and legible, separated from expressive graphics.
